Consult Summary:
Patient (27 y/o female) reports 2-day history of constant dull lower-abdominal ache with nausea and subjective feverishness; no vomiting. GP advised urgent same-day face-to-face review for examination, pregnancy test, and further investigations.

Problem List:

Issue 1: Lower-abdominal pain with nausea (2 days)
- Constant dull ache below umbilicus; started gradually 2 days ago.
- Associated: nausea, feeling hot/sweaty, subjective temperature rise.
- Denies vomiting, light-headedness, syncope.
- Bowel: constipated 1 week ago, now normal; last BM yesterday.
- GU: no vaginal discharge.
- Differential discussed: constipation vs other abdominal/pelvic pathology; pregnancy to be excluded.

Issue 2: Increased urinary frequency (same 2-day period)
- Drinks large amounts of water but notes increased voiding.
- Denies dysuria, urgency, foul smell, or hematuria.
- Slight pink tinge noticed in urine over last few days; unclear if menstrual spotting.
- No systemic UTI features mentioned (e.g., flank pain).

Issue 3: Gynecologic considerations
- LMP ≈ 3 weeks ago; period expected soon.
- Small amount of spotting/pink urine past couple of days.
- Sexually active with one partner; uses etonogestrel implant (Implanon) for contraception.
- Pregnancy not ruled out; GP to arrange pregnancy test and pelvic assessment.

Medications:
- Etonogestrel implant (Implanon) – dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- Amoxicillin – details of reaction not specified.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic illnesses reported.

Social History:
- Lives with boyfriend.
- Non-smoker.
- Alcohol intake not discussed.

Preventative History:
- No information provided on screenings or vaccinations.

Physical Examination:
- No face-to-face examination performed; no vitals recorded.

Plan:
- Arrange same-day face-to-face GP appointment for:
  • Abdominal and pelvic examination.
  • Urine dipstick and culture.
  • Pregnancy test.
  • Consider blood tests and imaging as indicated.
- Safety-net advice: if symptoms worsen, develop light-headedness, or new concerning features, seek urgent medical care.
- No prescriptions issued during teleconsult.
